hooks.text: A giant moon of Saturn vanished every time it orbited east.
One of Saturn's largest moons is shaped like a giant walnut.
Why did a massive moon of Saturn vanish every seventy-nine days?

title: The Bizarre Walnut Moon of Saturn
description: Saturn's moon Iapetus has a 12-mile-high equatorial ridge and two vastly different faces. Here is why Giovanni Cassini watched it vanish in 1671.

beats.text: A giant moon of Saturn vanished every time it orbited east.
beats.visual: Cassini spacecraft global mosaic of Iapetus showing two-tone albedo dichotomy, 2007

beats.text: In 1671, astronomer Giovanni Domenico Cassini tracked Iapetus on Saturn's western side, but lost it entirely on the east.
beats.visual: portrait of astronomer Giovanni Domenico Cassini, 17th century

beats.text: Cassini deduced that Iapetus was tidally locked, with one bright hemisphere and one dark hemisphere.
beats.visual: Cassini spacecraft view of Iapetus showing bright and dark halves, 2004

beats.text: Modern spacecraft proved him right: its trailing side gleams bright ice, while its leading face is coal-black.
beats.visual: Cassini closeup of transition boundary between dark terrain and bright ice, 2007

beats.text: Because Iapetus takes 79 days to rotate, thermal runaway strips ice into colder zones, leaving dark soot just one foot thick.
beats.visual: Cassini high-resolution image of dark Cassini Regio on Iapetus, 2007

beats.text: Then, in 2004, the Cassini probe revealed an equatorial mountain ridge towering 12 miles high.
beats.visual: Cassini spacecraft image of the equatorial mountain ridge on Iapetus, 2004

beats.text: This colossal mountain wall and bulging waistline give the two-toned moon the bizarre shape of a walnut.
beats.visual: Cassini global view showing walnut-shaped silhouette of Iapetus, 2007

beats.text: How would you explain a world that goes completely invisible on one side of its orbit?
beats.visual: Cassini mosaic showing both dark and bright faces of Iapetus, 2007

better_than_last: Replaced a closed summary with an open-ended question ending that flows directly back into the opening hook to maximize comments and replay loops.
